newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland in Ruch sale talks with several investors.
newsitem.headline: Poland in Ruch sale talks with several investors.

text.p: Poland's treasury ministry, which last week finished accepting new bids for kiosk chain Ruch SA, said on Monday it would continue talks with several potential investors.

"There have been several bids...our initial evaluations show that there will be more than two or three partners for more negotiations," deputy treasury minister Piotr Czyzewski told reporters at a seminar.
He declined to name the bidders.

The ministry launched a new tender for the privatisation of Ruch, which controls 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market, in March after withdrawing from a nearly ready deal with France's Hachette Distribution Service.
The new tender opened the way for a Polish group, led by Universal and including private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer Multico SA, to bid for Ruch.
The group, saying it would offer $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch and pledging to invest a total of $200 million in the company, placed its bid in the new tender.
Gazeta Wyborcza daily reported last week, quoting an anonymous sources, that Germany's Bertelsman was interested in buying Ruch.
Hachette, which ignored the new tender, plans to create its own distribution network in Poland if the government fails to sell it Ruch.
